title: Round 11 battery tests on the transposition-mixed keyword alphabets
why: Ideas 68, 70, 71 and 74 used the 220k plain keyword alphabets; round 10 showed the two transposition-mixed forms triple the alphabet set and are how a keyword alphabet is often built by hand.
plan: Re-run the tests of attacks 68 (clue alone / gap slack), 70 (mod 27-31), 71 part B (fixed multipliers) and 74 (keyed-lag autokey) with dictionary_alphabets(mixed=True), skipping alphabets already covered. Import the existing test functions rather than copying them. Keep 7+ checks, 3 shuffled controls, and one planted message per test built on a mixed alphabet. If the full set is too slow, run the ~cols and ~keyed forms of the theme and common words first and say so.

title: Gap slack for formula mining and the three-keyword join
why: Idea 68 showed nothing with the gap between the clues off by 1-3 letters, but only for the key-rule battery. Formula mining (54) and the Quagmire IV hash join (63) also tie the two clues together through absolute positions.
plan: For gap shifts -3..3 (excluding 0) move the second clue block's positions and re-run attack 54's formula search (sizes 0-3, position and grid ingredients only matter) and attack 63's hash join for key lengths 1-20. Reuse their functions with shifted position lists. Planted: a formula-key message with one ciphertext letter deleted between the clues. Controls: 2 shuffled K4s per shift.

title: German sentence keys on keyword tableaux
why: BERLIN CLOCK and the 1989 Berlin setting make German text a natural running key; attack 57 scored forced key fragments only against English.
plan: There is no German corpus in the repository and no network access is allowed, so first check data/ for any German text. If none exists, a German model cannot be built here: report verdict untestable and state exactly which file is needed (a German quadgram table). If a German model is present, re-run attack 57's fragment scoring with it on all keyword alphabets, 3 shuffled controls, planted German-key messages.

title: One deliberate wrong clue letter, for the round 9-11 exact tests
why: Sanborn's texts carry deliberate misspellings (IQLUSION, UNDERGRUUND, DESPARATLY). Round 7 tested one wrong clue letter only for periodic, two-key and Gromark models.
plan: For each of the 24 clue positions in turn, drop that position and re-run the key-rule battery (kryptos.round11.battery on the remaining 23 positions) over all keyword alphabets, the multiplier+adder solve (71 part A), and the rotor wire test (72, dictionary words). Require 7+ checks on the remaining letters. Compare the number of survivors with 3 shuffled K4s (each also with every drop). Planted: a sliding-key message with one clue letter changed.

title: Two paper rotors in series with hidden wirings
why: Idea 72 closed one rotor with hidden wiring. Two rotors is the smallest machine that idea cannot see, and the wire-collision test extends to it when the slow rotor moves rarely.
plan: Model C = R2[R1[P + s] - s + t] - t with the fast offset s from a constant speed or a dictionary word and the slow offset t constant inside each clue block (so each block is one single-rotor system with its own composite wiring). Test each block alone with the wire-collision test, then ask whether the two blocks' wirings are related by a shift t (conjugation of R2). Count forced coincidences honestly; say what key lengths are decidable. Planted two-rotor messages; 3 shuffled controls.

title: The S,S and R,R repeats as a device-independent constraint
why: The Wheatstone proof (idea 75) used only this: plain S then T gives cipher S,S at letters 32-33, and plain S ... T gives cipher R,R at letters 23 and 28. Any state machine must treat T after S,T,N,O,R as it treated S.
plan: Write the constraint down for general 'state advances by a function of the plaintext letter' ciphers: cipher = F(state), state += g(plain letter) mod m. The repeats give linear equations in the unknown increments g(S), g(T), g(N), g(O), g(R) mod m; add every other repeated cipher letter inside the clues (Q,Q; P,P; T,T; K; N; F; V). Solve for which moduli m in 2..60 any increment table exists at all, with and without requiring distinct cipher letters to mean distinct states. Report the surviving moduli; verify the solver on planted messages from such a device; run the same on shuffled K4s for the base rate.
